questions.questionText:
Sanjay is a risk taker and sets up a restaurant in Chennai. Sanjay works for the business as a
chef. He leases the restaurant building from Raghav and employs him to serve the customers.
Which income is earned by Sanjay and Raghav?
Sanjay Raghav

options.text: interest and profit wages only
interest and wages profits and rent
profits and wages rent and wages
profits only interest and wages

questions.questionText:
A government reduces social security spending by $10bn in order to increase defence spending
by $10bn.
What is this an example of?

options.text: expansionary fiscal policy
market forces
price stability
reallocation of resources

questions.questionText: What is included in macroeconomics?

options.text: the causes of a change in the price of one product
the causes of a market failure
the causes of determinants of price elasticities of supply
the causes of economic growth

questions.questionText: What is an advantage of a market economy in the allocation of resources?

options.text: It ensures that all consumers are willing to pay the same price.
It fixes prices based on costs of production.
It guarantees suppliers will make a profit.
It indicates the relative demand for goods and services.

questions.questionText:
106
What can be concluded from the data?

options.text: Prices fell between years 4 and 5.
Prices rose in every year.
The rate of inflation rose 5% in year 4.
There was a fall in living standards by year 5.

questions.questionText: Which characteristics of a product will cause market failure?

options.text: Information about the product is known equally by consumers and producers.
The consumption of the product has no external benefits.
The product is non-rival and non-excludable.
The production of the product has no external costs.

questions.questionText: Which function does a central bank provide for the general public?

options.text: accepting deposits
issuing banknotes
making loans
providing overdrafts

questions.questionText: What might cause a rise in wages?

options.text: a more elastic supply of labour
an increase in the size of the labour force
improved fringe benefits for workers
the introduction of a national minimum wage

questions.questionText:
A national trade union wishes to increase the wages of its members without reducing the
numbers employed.
Which factor would help the union to do this?

options.text: The demand for the industry’s product is increasing.
The industry consists of a small number of well-organised employers.
The union workers have low-level skills.
The workers’ wages are the largest cost of the industry.

questions.questionText: What will occur when there is a conglomerate merger?

options.text: increased control over supply of raw materials
increased risk-bearing economies of scale
reduced marketing economies of scale
reduced technical economies of scale

questions.questionText: What is total revenue?

options.text: the money received by the firm for each additional unit of output sold
the price of the good multiplied by the total quantity sold
the revenue per unit sold divided by the quantity sold
the revenue per unit sold minus the cost per unit sold

questions.questionText: How would a state-owned oil refining firm be classified?

options.text: as a multi-national company (MNC) in the private sector
as a private sector firm in the tertiary sector
as a public sector firm in the primary sector
as a public sector firm in the secondary sector

questions.questionText: What is included in a government’s budget?

options.text: the balance of government revenue and government expenditure
the balance of export revenue and import expenditure
the difference between investment and saving
the difference between social benefits and social costs of production

questions.questionText:
A country has rapidly increasing inflation.
What is an example of a monetary policy measure to reduce this problem?

options.text: increasing income tax
increasing interest rates
introducing maximum prices for some products
subsidising key industries

questions.questionText:
Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level.
What might cause deflation?

options.text: insufficient private capital investment
loss of confidence in the government’s economic policies
rising oil prices
shortages of skilled labour in relation to demand

questions.questionText:
Tax is charged at 1.45% on all wages earned to pay for basic medical provision.
How would this tax be described?

options.text: direct and proportional
direct and regressive
indirect and proportional
indirect and regressive

questions.questionText:
The table shows some data about an economy.
year 1
rate of inflation (%) 3.5
change in personal incomes (%) 2.5
What happened in year 1?

options.text: Both prices and real incomes fell.
Both prices and real incomes rose.
Prices fell but real incomes rose.
Prices rose but real incomes fell.

questions.questionText: What is included in the construction of the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)?

options.text: a base year
incomes
price elasticity of demand
quantity supplied

questions.questionText:
Which country is likely to have the highest standard of living?
infant mortality
birth rate death rate life expectancy
rate
Which statement about poverty is correct?

options.text: Absolute poverty occurs when income falls below what is needed for survival.
An advanced economy is likely to have a higher level of absolute poverty than relative poverty.
It is impossible for relative poverty to rise as absolute poverty falls.
Relative poverty is measured by the same goods and services in all countries.

questions.questionText:
The United Nations (UN) predicts that the population in low-income countries will increase.
What is likely to be a cause of this?

options.text: Climate change will lead to lower food output and starvation.
Improved education for girls will lead to a small decline in birth rates.
Increasing numbers of people will migrate to higher income countries.
Modern medicine and sanitation will lead to a rapid decline in death rates.

questions.questionText:
Which method of trade protection would enable domestic firms to lower their prices and undercut
the price of imported goods?

options.text: a subsidy
a tariff
an embargo
an import quota

questions.questionText: How might a multinational company (MNC) directly benefit a host country?

options.text: It creates local employment.
It depletes local natural resources.
It imports raw materials.
It receives tax concessions.

questions.questionText:
A country has a current account deficit on its balance of payments.
Which measure is most likely to reduce the deficit?

options.text: a cut in interest rates
a cut in the rate of income tax
a depreciation of the exchange rate
an increase in government expenditure

questions.questionText:
A country experienced a deficit on each of its trade in goods, primary income and secondary
income. Overall, it had a surplus on the current account of its balance of payments.
What must this mean?

options.text: It had a floating exchange rate.
It had a surplus on its trade in services.
It had a surplus on the government’s budget.

It was a low-income country.
